description: Glossary of 6529 terms projected from the site's curated help corpus. Each term links back to its help-index.json record via id.

aliases: can i use meme card art
facts: The License page lives at /about/license.
The Memes and Meme Lab NFTs are released by the artists under a Creative Commons 0 public-domain license to the maximum extent allowed by law.
The page says people can use The Memes and Meme Lab art for commercial or non-commercial purposes without seeking permission from the artists, subject to rights the artists do not control.
Gradient NFTs are treated differently: they have not been released under CC0, and the page warns against uses that could confuse people into thinking a product or service is offered by 6529.
Cards Collected is the total number of The Memes NFTs owned.
The Network Definitions page lists Cards Collected as a core Network metric.
A drop is a message posted in a wave.
Drops are written with the wave composer and can include text, markdown, mentions, emoji shortcodes, image uploads, and NFT hashtag references.
Depending on the wave type and rules, other members can react to, vote on, quote, reply to, boost, or pin drops.
Standard wave threads live at /waves/{waveId}; direct-message drops live at /messages/{waveId}.
EMMA is the Editor for Managing Multiphase Allowlists and the first reference implementation of Janus.
Opening /emma while signed in goes directly to /emma/plans, including with a restored session and no live wallet connection. A connected wallet alone is not a signed-in session.
Signed-out users at /emma see wallet guidance and a Connect wallet or Sign in action. Opening a plan while signed out preserves that plan destination through sign-in.

About EMMA, the question-mark link beside the title on the entry and plans pages, opens /emma/help. This public help page contains the full introduction, Janus link, TDH policy, and Back to EMMA link.
The distribution plan tool helps build mint plans with airdrops, allowlists, and public minting in one or more phases.
EMMA uses TDH as a lightweight anti-spam/rate-limit measure for allowlist creation.

In Create Snapshots at /emma/plans/{planId}, Use a 6529 collection presents five image rows: The Memes by 6529 (ERC1155), Meme Lab (ERC1155), 6529 Gradient (ERC721), 6529 RAW (ERC721), and 6529 Intern JPGs (ERC1155). Tab reaches each shortcut; Enter or Space selects it.

The Memes shortcut opens a season picker; choosing all or no seasons uses the full collection. Intern JPGs loads its subcollection token IDs. The other shortcuts fill name and contract address and clear old token IDs. Switching shortcuts preserves block numbers.

Or enter another collection keeps manual name and full contract address entry available, together with block number, optional token IDs, and optional consolidation block number. A full address can autofill an empty name. If metadata lookup fails, enter the name yourself. Collection-name search is unavailable.

The five shortcuts remain available without metadata lookup. If Intern JPG token IDs fail to load or are empty, the form stays unchanged and shows an error. Select the shortcut to retry, or enter its name, contract address, and token IDs manually; leaving token IDs empty selects all tokens in the shared contract.
Genesis Sets are complete sets of the first three Meme NFTs.
Genesis Sets appear in Network Definitions and are also referenced by TDH Category B boost rules.
Groups are reusable community/member sets used across app workflows such as waves.
On Network, open Filter to create and apply a criteria-based group. The Network filter does not offer Choose group.
Criteria-based groups are created inline from workflows such as Network filtering and Wave setup; there is no standalone Network Groups page.
A profile's Groups tab remains available at /{user}/groups.
Meme Sets means the number of complete sets of The Memes owned, across all SZNs or for a specific SZN.
The Network Definitions page lists Meme Sets as a core Network metric.
Meme Sets -1 and Meme Sets -2 are complete Meme sets missing 1 or 2 cards respectively.
Use this definition when users ask about near-complete Meme sets.
Nakamoto Set is a SZN1 Category B TDH boost term.
Under current TDH 1.4 rules, SZN1 can use a complete set boost or the Genesis Set and Nakamoto Set boosts.

Holding Nakamoto (Meme #4) adds the configured Nakamoto partial-set bonus when SZN1 is boostable and incomplete. The complete SZN1 boost replaces its partial-set bonuses. See Current boosts at /network/tdh#tdh-1-4 for the current API-derived amount.
Network definitions explain Cards Collected, Unique Memes, Meme Sets, TDH variants, purchases, sales, transfers, and related Network metrics.
The glossary groups terms into Collection metrics, Activity metrics, and TDH metrics.
Genesis Sets are complete sets of the first three Meme NFTs.
Use the definitions page when users ask what a Network metric means.
For a single TDH explanation, point users to the TDH page.
Network Levels are an integrated signal based on TDH and REP.
The levels page presents its explanation above a full-width table of all Level 0 through 100 thresholds.
When a signed-in active profile is available, the levels page shows its current Level, combined TDH and REP, next Level, and additional amount needed; an active proxy profile takes precedence.
Signed-out users and users whose profile data is unavailable see the general reference page without a personalized empty state or calculator.
Levels are shown across profile and Network surfaces where relevant.
Network wave score has a dedicated route at /network/wave-score.

In the app, the score page has a Back button in the header. It returns to the originating page when supplied, including Discover sort and threshold settings; otherwise it uses app navigation history, or About on a direct visit with no history.
Use this route when users ask where wave score information lives.
Wave REP is a TDH-credit REP signal for a wave; it is signed and log-scaled before weighting in Wave Score.
Wave REP is the largest single quality component on the Wave Score transparency page.
Raw Wave REP can be very large or very negative; the score maps it to a bounded component for discovery math.
Wave-specific participation remains under individual wave routes.
The Profile Brain tab surfaces Brain-related profile activity and wave context.

The profile Brain drop feed, including replies, shows only posts from publicly viewable waves. Private waves and direct messages are excluded even when the viewer can access them; subwaves require both the subwave and parent to be publicly viewable. Viewer-specific reactions, bookmarks, and votes remain available while signed in.
Brain views include activity and wave sidebar surfaces where available.

Created Waves lists accessible non-direct-message root waves and subwaves created by the profile, ordered by that profile's latest post in each wave; waves without a qualifying profile post appear after active waves.
When a profile has no accessible created waves, the Created Waves section is omitted instead of showing an empty message.
Recently Active In lists accessible non-direct-message root waves and subwaves ordered by the profile's latest post, whether or not the profile created them; a wave can appear in both sections.

Each row labels the profile-specific time as Last post. Created Waves also labels its separate total wave posts count, which includes retained CHAT posts by all authors; Recently Active In does not show that wave-wide total.
Created Waves initially shows five rows on desktop, and both lists provide Load more controls so cursor pages remain reachable.
On desktop, Created Waves and Recently Active In share one independently scrollable sidebar, so scrolling it does not advance the Brain feed.
On small screens, More opens the Created waves modal with the same profile-specific ordering and Load more pagination; it does not show a partial page count as a total.
When a focused Load more control retrieves the final cursor page, focus moves to an All waves loaded status so keyboard focus is preserved.
Created Waves and Recently Active In load and recover independently, and results refresh for a connected-viewer change so private-wave access is not reused across viewers.
Use /{user}/brain for profile-specific Brain context.
The combined Identity tab is the default profile tab at /{user}; /{user}/identity is a legacy redirect.
NIC is the 6529 network identity trust signal shown on profile identity surfaces.
App copy expands NIC as Network Identity Check (D142) in both the About FAQ and the profile identity header.
The Identity tab surfaces profile identity, REP behavior, NIC ratings, NIC statements, and activity log behavior where available.

On mobile, grouped text-only REP, NIC, and ID Statements buttons switch sections without changing the profile URL. The buttons have no numbers. REP and NIC show Received/Given beside the content heading and the selected total below. The statement count appears inside ID Statements.
Grant Rep keeps its compact category pills and existing search and selection behavior, including similarly named categories remaining separate and selectable.

On desktop, Grant Rep, Rate NIC and REP contributor lists retain their top alignment about 14% down the viewport. NIC lists start about 10% down, are at most 560px wide and 80% of the viewport height, and scroll inside while the owner footer stays visible. Mobile keeps the draggable bottom sheets and safe-area padding.

The REP categories summary says You assigned: with the same grouped integer format as Total REP, without a plus sign and with a minus sign only for negative values. On mobile and medium screens, this summary stays beside Grant Rep as a group at the right of the category heading. When space is tight, the summary moves below the button and stays right-aligned.

The exact MemesNominee category pill is marked as counting toward the 50,000 REP submission requirement and is surfaced first when the typed value differs only by capitalization, spacing, punctuation, or Unicode width; search guidance stays neutral until a category is selected, selecting exact MemesNominee confirms the requirement in green, and selecting a subdued look-alike shows an amber note explaining that it remains a separate category.

In the Grant Rep and Rate NIC dialogs, type the desired total, including any existing contribution. REP and NIC amount inputs show locale-aware digit grouping while unfocused and plain digits while editing, without changing the saved value. The plus/minus symbols are informational, not buttons. Use Grant Rep or Save to save, or Cancel to leave without saving.

REP category tags open a contributor list inline on desktop or in a draggable bottom sheet on mobile and the native app. The labeled Open category ↗ action opens the global category view; it sits on the left of the footer when there are no unsaved changes, on desktop and mobile. Eligible members viewing another profile see their pinned You row first only where they already have a nonzero contribution, including negative REP. On desktop its amount is focused on opening without selecting the digits; mobile keeps the sheet title focused without opening the keyboard. Use Grant Rep to add REP where no contribution exists. Own Received, signed-out and unauthorized views are read-only. In your own Given category outside proxy mode, edit receiver amounts together as the main way to adjust REP, using the same allowance and save rules as the full receiver list. Typed negative totals are supported; zero removes a rating. Changed values reveal Cancel and Save. Enter saves; Escape cancels a draft, then closes the list. Saving refreshes totals, counts and activity. After the full save succeeds, the mobile and native category sheet closes, dismisses the keyboard and returns focus to the category tag; the desktop expandable stays open. While REP saves, the header and drag handle stay in place, with Back, Close, Escape and dragging temporarily disabled to avoid a layout jump. A failed or partially saved batch keeps the sheet open with remaining edits available to retry. Category tags keep their order while a panel or sheet is open, so the editor does not jump when totals change. Closing it restores the current ranking by total. Failed edits stay for retry while successful writes are kept.

On desktop, Received and Given REP categories use the same compact tags, arranged side by side and wrapping as needed. The open tag keeps its size and position; an 8px filled bridge joins it to the full-width contributor panel below its row. Tags and panels have subtle fills. Tags have a faint border that strengthens slightly on hover, while the joined panel has no outline. The contributor count appears only in the tag. The panel footer shows the current total, an arrow and the proposed total without crossing either amount out. Only one category is open at a time; mobile and native use the existing bottom sheet.

REP category tags show up to three profile avatars followed by the full rater or receiver count. When signed in and viewing another profile, a nonzero personal amount also appears on the tag after a subtle dot: You assigned in Received, and Assigned to you in Given. Your own profile omits these personal labels from summaries and tags in both directions. Each category total appears once; in your own Given view it is the total you assigned across that category’s receivers. Amounts use grouped integers with a minus sign when negative. Narrow tags place this amount on a second line with vertical padding and a gap below the title. Wider full-row tags place it beside the category name and total, with contributor avatars and count kept at the right. Tags grow to fit the personal amount comfortably. Category avatars are 24px. On desktop, hovering an avatar enlarges it and shows the profile name and REP contribution; clicking it opens that profile. The rest of the tag opens the category list. On touch devices, tapping anywhere on the tag, including an avatar, opens the list; profiles are linked inside the list. Avatars beside the REP and NIC summary totals still link directly to profiles. There is no separate edit pencil; permitted adjustments are made in the open panel.
On mobile, REP category sheets fit above the keyboard and scroll the focused amount into view after the keyboard settles.

REP and NIC have Received/Given views on desktop and mobile. NIC Received shows incoming score, status and raters; Given shows outgoing NIC and receivers. In both REP and NIC summaries, avatars open individual profiles. The matching borderless rater or receiver count buttons and chevrons open the full lists. Owners can adjust their Given ratings there. Received and Given rating lists fit their contents up to the same maximum height; longer lists scroll inside the dialog. The selected mobile REP and NIC totals appear in the content, and show a dash while unavailable. On mobile, Rate NIC sits on the right of the raters summary row when rating is permitted. Your existing NIC rating stays beside the button when there is room, or below it and right-aligned when space is tight.

On your own profile outside proxy mode, open Given then select the receiver count and chevron. REP keeps its receiver list: a linked handle, total and Adjust action per person, without expanding categories under everyone. The summary receiver count is unique identities, not category allocations. Someone with REP in several categories counts once overall and once per applicable category, so category counts need not add up to the summary. Adjust opens that receiver's existing categories, then the selected category's amount form. Back returns one step and preserves the loaded list and scroll; Cancel closes without saving. On desktop and mobile, a successful REP Save closes the entire receiver-management dialog or bottom sheet and returns focus to the receiver-count button. Reopening shows the refreshed first page. Failed saves keep the editor open with the draft. The category tag expanders remain the main way to adjust several receivers together. Highest total first and Most recently adjusted retain their original sorting; Load more continues in pages of 25. REP Received shows raters and totals read-only. Owners and visitors can sort Received and Given with Highest total first or Most recently adjusted. Sorting does not grant editing permissions. Overview category ordering stays unchanged.

Expandable REP categories and the NIC receiver list use editable amount boxes with grouped idle numbers and plain digits on focus, without automatically selecting them. Changed rows show a signed adjustment; increases use emerald and decreases use rose, including the proposed footer total. One footer shows available credit or Total before → after with Cancel and Save. NIC edits stay in the refreshed receiver list after saving; Cancel resets drafts in place. Confirmed writes are kept after a later failure, and failed edits remain for retry. Close discards drafts and exits; Escape resets drafts, then closes. Signed whole numbers are supported, zero removes a rating, and Save is disabled for invalid or over-budget changes. NIC keeps its green Save. While saving, Close stays visible but disabled so the sheet header stays steady. New REP categories stay with Grant Rep; standalone Grant Rep and Rate NIC remain unchanged.

Rating lists support loading, empty, retry and Load more states. REP keeps contributor counts in the profile summary; NIC also shows the count above its rows. Received and Given share subtle row backgrounds, avatar and handle styling, with amounts aligned right. Read-only values are plain numbers; eligible editors have inputs in the category editor and NIC list. REP receiver management retains Adjust. Linked handles change color on hover without an underline. Mobile NIC and expandable REP category editors use 44px amount boxes and buttons and keep the footer visible above the safe area and software keyboard. The mobile REP total and receiver summary share one line. Existing proxy allocation flows are unchanged.
Owner and permission rules affect which identity actions are visible.
The Profile Proxy tab exposes profile proxy relationships and actions.
All, Received, and Granted filters remain visible as tabs on phone, tablet, and desktop. Arrow keys switch tabs; Home and End select the first and last tab.
Proxy features help a profile allow another account to perform supported actions without handing over the primary wallet.

To act as a received proxy, open your account menu and select the profile under Proxy Profile. If the wallet is disconnected, reconnect the wallet belonging to your signed-in profile; the selected proxy resumes and asks for a sign-in signature. On an unsupported network, switch to a supported network and select the profile again. Your current session and selection stay in place until sign-in succeeds. Canceling or a failed sign-in shows an error. Select your own profile under Proxy Profile to return to the primary profile, which also requires signing in.
Current proxy action creation supports Allocate Rep and Allocate NIC actions with a granted Credit amount and read-only Spent total.
Proxy action availability and profile rating behavior depend on whether the active proxy has the relevant Allocate Rep or Allocate NIC permission.
Proxy and delegation are related concepts but live in separate product areas.
Quick Tags are managed from the compact owner-only section beneath Activity on the Profile Brain tab.
The section shows up to three tags and uses a +N more chip when additional tags exist; controls wrap at narrow widths.
Manage and +N more open the inline Quick Tags manager inside the same Brain-tab card.
On mobile, New Quick Tag and existing-tag editing open in a bottom sheet; on wider screens, create and edit forms remain inline.
The mobile Quick Tag editor uses Back, Close, or a downward header swipe to discard edits. The inline editor keeps Cancel.
The section is hidden on other profiles and while acting through a proxy.
Quick Tags do not have a dedicated profile tab or route.
Purchases and Sales count bought and sold NFTs for Memes or Gradients.
Purchases (ETH) and Sales (ETH) show ETH spent or received for those NFTs.
REP is peer-given reputation in categories and waves.
CIC is the community interaction count signal shown on profiles and Network surfaces.
REP category analytics and category-level views live under /rep/categories.

On devices without touch, profile hover cards show up to three Top Rep categories ordered by the magnitude of their net REP total, so a large negative can appear first. Equal magnitudes use case-sensitive category-name order. Signed values and their positive, negative, or zero colors are preserved.

Safe Collecting at /safe-collecting (formerly the Delegation Center) explains and sets up 6529's safe collecting system: keep NFTs in a vault that never connects to anything, and use 6529 from a hot wallet, while TDH, delegations, airdrops and subscriptions keep working as if every wallet were one.

The former /delegation URLs permanently redirect to the equivalent /safe-collecting pages, preserving query parameters and section anchors. Wallet Architecture is now /safe-collecting/tap-guide, and the FAQ and its articles are under /safe-collecting/faq.

It follows the Three Address Protocol (TAP): a vault (ideally a SAFE with hardware-wallet signers, or a hardware wallet) that holds NFTs and never connects; a transaction wallet on a hardware wallet that buys, sells and trades and acts as the vault's Delegation Manager; a hot social wallet that signs in to 6529, votes, posts, mints and pays for subscriptions and holds no NFTs; and optionally an old, burned or exposed address kept combined for its TDH.

The recommended setup for new collectors: the vault signs once to set its ENS name and appoint the transaction wallet as Delegation Manager (use case 998) on Any Collection; the guided setup combines the wallets with the manager signing for the vault; optionally the manager delegates minting to the social wallet; airdrops without a delegation go to the wallet with the most TDH, usually the vault.

When a wallet is connected, the Your setup section lists the profile's wallets with TDH, primary and connected badges, which wallet manages which, minting and airdrop delegations, and a checklist with links to fix missing steps.

The page links to every tool: guided consolidation, appointing a manager, minting and airdrop delegations, primary address, locks, revoking, and the Wallet Checker. The original delegation, consolidation and Delegation Manager forms and Manage by Collection are under All tools.

A Delegation Manager cannot move NFTs but can register anything in the vault's name, including consolidations and more managers; an expiry date does not limit it, only revoking does, and revoking it does not undo what it registered.
TDH means Total Days Held.
TDH does not stand for Total Dynamic Head.
TDH is 6529's time-weighted holding metric for eligible NFTs.
Conceptually, TDH measures long-term participation and skin in the 6529 ecosystem.
Each eligible NFT contributes value based on how long it has been held; that base holding time is then adjusted by edition-size weighting and by collection boosters.

FirstGM (Meme #8) was designed to establish the one-TDH reference: one copy held for one complete day earns one base TDH before boosts. Its open-mint design is central to its role as the original reference card, explained near the start of the TDH page at #tdh-reference.

Ordinary burns do not reduce the minted count used for TDH edition weighting. FirstGM (Meme #8) has a fixed exception that subtracts 2,588 from its 6,529 minted copies, giving 3,941 before the edition-size floor is applied.
The calculation has three layers: unweighted days, edition weighting, and boosts.
Unweighted days means each NFT contributes 1 unit per day it is held.
Edition weighting means days held are multiplied by a HODL or edition-size rate. The calculator derives rates from the largest eligible effective Meme edition.

An edition-size floor is a minimum count used for TDH: when fewer copies were minted, the calculation uses the floor instead. The exact calculation section explains how floors are set and gives a worked example.
Boosts multiply weighted TDH by active boosters based on what the holder owns.
The TDH page has anchors for FirstGM's reference role, a fixed worked example, profile lookup, current boosts, and exact calculation details.
The worked example compares Today and +30 days and can remove Nakamoto #4 before the snapshot; it demonstrates that a sale removes both the card contribution and any boost component it supplied.

Profile lookup accepts a public handle or wallet-like identity without requiring wallet authentication, and shows loading, empty, not-found, retryable error, snapshot, holdings, boost breakdown, and paginated collection states.
The daily snapshot uses the Ethereum block at or immediately before 00:00 UTC; holding age uses that block timestamp, while a displayed API date can reflect later processing time.
The current boost is deterministic for a particular snapshot once eligible cards, ownership history, rates, and season configuration are known; future inputs can still change the result.

The Current boosts section at /network/tdh#tdh-1-4 loads configured bonus amounts, boosted-season limits, additional-set decay and Gradient limits from GET /tdh/rules. Consult that section for current values and the future schedule.
The highest eligible season is excluded from season boosts; later seasons do not automatically extend the configured boosted-season limit.
A full eligible Meme collection uses the configured season sum plus geometrically diminishing bonuses for additional full sets, with no hard set-count cap.

Distinct Gradients add the configured per-token bonus up to the configured count limit. The page derives the eventual rounded multiplier ceiling from the full season schedule, additional-set series and Gradient limit.
The displayed future ceiling is conditional: future cards must become eligible and can make a previously complete collection incomplete.
Rates are rounded before wallet and token-level TDH rounding; consolidated wallets preserve qualifying internal-transfer ages, recompute the boost, and sum per-token rounded final contributions.
TDH is used throughout the network, including profiles, leaderboards, Levels, groups, Network views, Waves voting and eligibility, and public data.
TDH ranks are consecutive positions starting at 1; equal displayed TDH does not give wallets or consolidations a shared rank.
Overall TDH ranks compare boosted TDH, unboosted TDH, Gradients TDH and NextGen TDH, in that order, highest first.

Memes, Gradients and NextGen collection ranks compare that collection's boosted TDH, unboosted TDH and NFT balance, then total NFT balance, highest first. Owners of an individual Meme card compare that card's TDH, then total boosted TDH, highest first.

A complete tie uses the lowercase wallet address in ascending order, or the consolidation key made from lowercase wallet addresses sorted in ascending order and joined with hyphens. Backend and native 6529 Desktop use the same ranking rules; tie-breaks change positions without changing holdings, TDH scores or boosts.
Individual Gradient and NextGen token rankings compare token TDH highest first, then numeric token ID lowest first.

A collection rank of -1 means there is no positive boosted TDH for that collection. Empty singleton wallets are omitted from TDH rankings; wallets with eligible NFTs or membership in a multi-wallet consolidation remain included even when TDH is zero.
TDH (unboosted) is TDH weighted by edition size before boosters are applied.

FirstGM (Meme #8) was designed as the original one-TDH reference: one copy held for one complete day earns one base TDH before boosts. The calculator derives edition rates from the largest eligible effective Meme edition.
TDH (unweighted) is Total Days Held summed daily at 00:00 UTC.
In unweighted TDH, each NFT contributes one unit per day held before edition weighting or boosters.
The Memes is the main Meme Card collection area.
Use The Memes routes to browse cards, card pages, distributions, and minting-related surfaces.
Individual Meme Card pages and distribution pages live under The Memes route family.
The Memes collection routes are separate from Memes wave submission surfaces in Waves.

The Memes subscriptions are an optional way to mint eligible Meme Cards remotely without being online at mint time, with estimated gas savings of about 80% for one card and up to 98% for ten cards funded by one ETH transfer.
Subscriptions are not a mintpass and do not create extra allowlist access.
The setup path is: connect a wallet, open the profile Subscriptions tab, add a completely non-refundable ETH balance, choose Automatic or Manual mode, and select or skip upcoming eligible cards.
The /about/subscriptions primary action says Connect to Subscribe when a wallet or profile handoff is needed and Manage when the user can continue to their profile subscription settings.
Users manage their subscription mode, balance, airdrop address, top-ups, upcoming drops, and history under their profile Subscriptions tab.

On desktop, Subscription History is a separate section with Redeemed, Log History and Top Up History pills. Below 1024px, the Subscription History row opens the same tabs and records in the shared bottom sheet. Selection and pagination are preserved during refreshes and resizing.
Automatic mode mints eligible cards until the balance is used unless the user opts out; Manual mode only mints cards the user opts into.
Automatic mode does not expire when the balance is insufficient; coverage describes what the current balance funds, not an expiration date for the mode.

Coverage counts consecutive fully funded intended drops from the immediate next intended drop and accounts for mode, eligibility, edition preference, selections, opt-outs, balance, and the published schedule.
Coverage is Covered at 7 or more consecutive fully funded intended drops, Plan a top up at 4 to 6, Running low at 2 to 3, and Action required at 0 to 1. These existing thresholds are unchanged.

When available, Funded through identifies the funded-through Meme and full date. Upcoming Drops shows one amber Funded through boundary after the last funded drop, or Next unfunded before the supplied next unfunded drop when there is no funded-through point. Selection switches and visitor subscription statuses keep their existing meaning. Next unfunded stays in the summary facts when no deadline line already names the same drop. Owners see the supplied top-up deadline once in the summary; Top up shows the recommended amount and funding projection without repeating the deadline. Original date formats, including years and UTC cutoff times, are preserved.
If an eligible card is unavailable, no card is airdropped and the unused balance stays available.
The About Subscriptions overview links to the Subscriptions Report for aggregate subscribed and redeemed subscription counts.
Transfers In and Transfers Out are NFTs moved into or out of an address.
The Network Definitions page lists transfers as a core Network activity metric.
Unique Memes is the total number of unique Meme NFTs owned.
Use Unique Memes when comparing breadth of holdings rather than total card count.
Waves are the main social threads for conversations, drops, reactions, voting, and wave-specific activity.
Standard wave threads live at /waves/{waveId}; direct messages live at /messages/{waveId}.
Public wave content can remain readable for authenticated wallets without a profile, but posting and other participation actions require profile setup.

The Waves panel includes independently collapsible Active Votes and Worth Checking Out sections, All/Pinned/Joined collection controls in a dark segmented group that fills the row beside search, with equally wide 30px tabs in a 36px group on desktop, 34px tabs in a 40px group on touch devices, compact normal-weight labels, a larger 44px touch tap area, a subtle border and a filled selected option, with a transparent search icon to their right, a feed shortcut, and create controls. Signed-out visitors see an All Waves label on the left and the same search icon on the right, without personal collection tabs. Wave search spans all accessible non-DM waves regardless of the selected collection. Click the search icon to reveal and focus Find a wave search. The field replaces the tabs while open. On touch devices, the focused search field scrolls into view. In the native app, the Waves list resizes above the keyboard to keep search and results reachable, then restores its height when the keyboard closes. A small spinner appears in the input while a query is waiting or fetching; the close button or Escape clears search, hides the field, and restores the selected collection. Refresh clears this sidebar search and restores the last selected All, Pinned or Joined collection. The selected collection shows a small spinner while its data is loading. Wallet and profile restoration keep an empty collection pending even before an address is available. After resolution, a genuinely empty guest or connected list can show its empty message.
On desktop with no selected Wave, /waves shows the latest posts from members' effective public Profile Wave curations, newest first.

Each latest-profile-post card identifies the author, posting time, and originating Profile Wave; curated replies can also appear. On mobile web and in the native app, the default /waves view remains a Wave navigator with no separate Profile Waves Feed card, and the feed icon at the far right of the plain Waves heading opens the cross-Wave feed at /waves?view=profile-feed. On desktop, the same feed icon clears the selected wave to show Profile Waves Feed. The heading is not clickable. Header actions are feed then create on desktop, with Profile Waves Feed and Create Wave tooltips. The Profile Waves Feed header shortcut uses the same transparent icon style and rounded corners on desktop and smaller screens, with a larger touch target. Create uses a solid white button with a plus icon and visible Create wave label in the expanded desktop sidebar; the collapsed rail keeps a plus icon named Create wave. The mobile web list shows feed then the labeled Create wave button; the native app list shows only feed and keeps create in its top bar. The Profile Waves Feed content header has a Discover Waves link with a compass, aligned right on desktop and below the description on small screens. The expanded sidebar has no separate feed row.
From the mobile web Profile Waves Feed, Waves returns to the Wave list. Opening a feed post enters its Wave conversation, and browser Back returns to the feed.

The collapsed desktop rail shows Profile Waves Feed as a borderless dark tile. Expanded header utilities, including the feed shortcut, search, clock and sidebar toggles, are transparent at rest with a dark hover surface and blue keyboard focus. The selected desktop feed icon and open sidebar toggle stay blue. Create wave and Join keep solid white primary styling; Add REP, Joined, and View subwaves retain bordered secondary styling.

Announcements uses a compact row with its timestamp, unread state and score shield. With collapsed replies, its timestamp shows the latest top-level announcement; replies neither advance that timestamp nor increase the wave unread badge. A row-sized placeholder reserves its space while it first loads. Expanded wave rows and Active Votes show a shield beside the muted score number; selecting the score opens its details. Keyboard focus remains visible, and hover brightens the score. The current wave highlights in Active Votes as well as in the collection list below when it appears in both. In Worth Checking Out, each avatar and its bottom-right score shield form one wave navigation link; hovering or focusing the combined link shows score details.

While Find a wave is open, sidebar scores remain visible but their details cards are temporarily unavailable, including for an empty search field. Closing search restores score hover, focus and selection. Recommendation links remain available while searching.
Every Worth Checking Out recommendation also appears in All at its recent-activity position; Joined normally includes only waves the user has joined.

All includes pinned, joined, unjoined, and quiet accessible waves. Expand a parent to reach its subwaves. Stable batches prevent new activity from skipping waves while scrolling. Scroll near the bottom or choose Load more waves. Failed loads retain existing rows and offer Retry. Expired lists refresh automatically; newly created or newly accessible waves appear on refresh. Every batch rechecks access permissions.

Joined waves load in batches without skipping entries when new activity changes their order. Recent activity includes joined, unmuted subwaves. Muting a wave removes its own activity from the ordering. In Joined, pinned waves appear when their batch loads; older pins do not appear ahead of unloaded joined waves. Pinned shows saved pins without loading more of Joined. More rows load near the bottom, with Load more joined waves as a fallback. Failed loads keep existing rows available and show Retry. Expired lists refresh automatically, and newly joined waves appear on refresh.
Switching All and Joined preserves list position instead of jumping to the active wave; a shorter list can clamp the position. Selecting another wave reveals its active row again.

Incoming messages update badges and recent-activity ordering without moving the Waves list's scroll position, including messages in the open wave. Opening another wave reveals its row once after the list loads; later messages do not scroll to it again. Desktop pointer devices have a slim scrollbar for dragging and track clicks; touch devices keep native scrolling.

A Wave opened from a direct link remains visible and highlighted in the left sidebar even when it is not followed, pinned, or present in the loaded overview; this temporary route context does not join or pin it.

When a direct link opens a subwave, the sidebar surfaces its visible parent, loads and expands the subwave list, reveals the selected child row, and keeps that parent tree ahead of paginated activity rows so every sibling remains reachable.
An active subwave header shows an up-left arrow and a linked parent wave name; selecting that name opens the parent wave.

Pin and unpin check the selected profile session before changing the list. If the session cannot renew, reconnect that wallet and retry; a failed session check leaves the pin state unchanged. Public waves can remain readable after session expiry but are not added to saved pins. Failed server pin changes roll back and show an error.
xTDH is an extension of TDH that lets TDH-like network participation flow beyond core 6529 holders to other NFT holders and communities.
xTDH can be earned by holding eligible cards outside The Memes ecosystem.
The frontend /network/xtdh page is labeled xTDH Overview and describes xTDH as an extension of TDH that helps include other NFT holders in the 6529 ecosystem and offer them the benefits of TDH.
xTDH tracks how much xTDH your Memes produce, how much xTDH you receive from grants on tokens you own, and how much xTDH you have granted away.
Produced xTDH comes from TDH production: produced_xTDH_today = TDH gained today * xTDH_coefficient.
The current backend coefficient is 0.1.
Daily xTDH rate is xtdh_rate = produced_today - granted_out_today + received_today.
Total xTDH accumulates as xtdh_total = xtdh_total_previous + xtdh_rate.
The key idea is grants: a profile that produces xTDH can grant future xTDH flow to all tokens in an external ERC-721 collection or to a selected subset of tokens.

To select a collection in Create New Grant, paste its Ethereum contract address (0x followed by 40 hexadecimal characters), select the ERC-721 result, then choose all tokens, individual IDs, or ranges. Collection-name search, ENS names, and marketplace URLs are not supported for this lookup.
If collection metadata fails to load, use Try again. A missing or non-ERC-721 result cannot be selected. Contract metadata lookup is not a spam or authenticity check.
If you own a token with an active grant, you receive your share of that grant while you own the token.

Per-token grant flow is grant_amount_per_token = rate / denominator, where the denominator is either the collection total supply for full-collection grants or the number of selected tokens for partial grants.
Transfers inside the same consolidation group do not reset the ownership window; sales or transfers across groups do reset it.
The first grant increment requires the grant and token ownership to have matured past the required midnight or 24-hour windows.

xTDH is not simply TDH for external NFTs; it is a grant and allocation layer where TDH producers create xTDH, can grant future production outward, external token owners can receive it, and ungranted or ineligible flow remains with the grantor.
No produced xTDH is intended to disappear; it is allocated to someone.
For live network-wide xTDH allocation data, use the xTDH Allocations Dashboard at /xtdh.
Profile xTDH information is available under /{user}/xtdh when visible.
